articles.title: Flathead on the move and bream biting in Mallacoota's top lake
body: This week's East Gippsland fishing round-up says flathead are moving around Mallacoota, with paddle-tail soft plastics working along the edges of the sandy flats. The top lake is reported to be fishing exceptionally well for bream, with bass yabbies and prawns producing fish for anglers in boats and on the shore. Elsewhere in the region, bream are the main target in the rivers and salmon and gummy shark are turning up along the surf beaches.

articles.title: 167 bird species in October, a district first, and new Hooded Plover chicks
body: Mallacoota district observers recorded 167 bird species in October, well above the usual October count and only one short of 2025's 168. The Glossy Ibis was the bird of the month and a first record for the district, and the month also brought Pacific Koel, Channel-billed Cuckoo, Australian Shelduck with very young ducklings at the treatment plant, and an emu on Genoa Road. Activity included a Birdlife East Gippsland campout, a Friends of Mallacoota weeding trip to Gabo Island and a Hooded Plover banding team. One of the banded plovers, green flag "AL", hatched three chicks with its mate on 29 October.
Source: Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife, 31 October 2026, https://mallacootaweatherwildlife.blogspot.com/2026/10/october-2026-bird-report.html

articles.title: East Gippsland and Bega Valley councils meet in Mallacoota
body: East Gippsland Shire and Bega Valley Shire councillors and senior staff held a full-day regional summit in Mallacoota last week. East Gippsland mayor Cr Jodie Ashworth hosted Bega Valley mayor Cr Russell Fitzpatrick and his delegation. Because the two councils share the state border, they face many of the same problems, especially emergency management, ongoing bushfire recovery and delivering services across long distances, and the day was spent comparing notes on community support, resilience and infrastructure. The visit ended with site inspections of local projects and recovery work around town, and both councils said they would keep working together and sharing resources across the Victoria-NSW border.

articles.title: Wet, warm October: 128mm of rain and a +1.8°C anomaly
body: Mallacoota's October was wet and warm, according to the monthly report from local weather station keeper Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife. The station recorded 128.1mm for the month, well above the 91.8mm at the BoM airport gauge, suggesting storm cells focused on the Inlet rather than the coast; the peak rain rate was 73.8mm/hr during the 25 October storm. Temperatures ran 1.8°C above average, with a top of 31.7°C on the 12th and a five-day hot spell from 20 to 24 October.
Source: Mallacoota Weather and Wildlife, 3 Nov 2026, https://mallacootaweatherwildlife.blogspot.com/2026/11/october-2026-mallacoota-weather-report.html

articles.title: Mallacoota Flatty Classic top 10 leaderboard: Nickbar on top
body: The Mallacoota Flatty Classic's top 10 leaderboard has been published in this week's Snowy River Mail sport scoreboard. Team Nickbar heads the field on 1,489 points, ahead of Bent Tips on 1,454 and Anger Management on 1,444, with Another Job (1,392) and Liquor Legends (1,330) rounding out the top five. The rest of the top 10 were separated by less than 120 points, with Fishy Business in tenth on 1,206.

articles.title: Reel It In Flathead Challenge returns to Mallacoota 13-15 November
body: The Reel It In Mallacoota Flathead Challenge is back next weekend, Friday 13 to Sunday 15 November. Teams of two to four anglers fish artificial lures only across Saturday and Sunday, with registration at the Mallacoota Hotel on Friday afternoon (4-6pm) and day codes handed out outside Cafe 54 each morning. First place for a team of four is listed at a minimum $8000 in prizes, and results also count toward the new Anaconda Southern Series.

articles.title: Greencape Road closed for bridge repairs
body: Greencape Road is closed for about eight weeks while the bridge is repaired. The detour starts 4 km down Edrom Road, then along [Duckhole Road](https://www.google.com/maps?q=-37.140263,149.922852), which is in decent shape. The [turnoff to the lighthouse](https://www.google.com/maps?q=-37.175726,149.900153) is on the way, and Green Cape itself is [2086 Green Cape Road, Green Cape NSW 2551](https://www.google.com/maps?q=-37.261082,150.049493).
